title: Stronger rules on third-party litigation funding proposed
summary: The SRA has proposed new rules for firms that use or arrange third-party litigation funding. Most apply only to consumer claims, but core conduct duties would apply to all funded claims. The consultation closed on 17 September 2026.
what_changes: For any type of funded claim, firms would have to stay independent of funders and share client information only with informed consent.
For consumer claims, firms would have to notify the SRA and give clients a funding information document before they sign a funding agreement.
Firms would have to keep a funding risk assessment, updated every six months and approved by the firm's head and compliance officers.
Some firms would also need an orderly closure plan. Personal injury, clinical negligence and CAT collective actions are excluded.
who_it_applies_to: SRA-regulated firms that use or arrange third-party litigation funding. Most proposals cover consumer claims only, excluding personal injury and clinical negligence.

history.event: Consultation opened, running until 17 September 2026; new guidance on current obligations published at the same time.
Consultation closed on 17 September 2026. The SRA is analysing responses before deciding whether to seek LSB approval.
